title: Fix the Brackets by Deleting as Few as Possible

concept.title: Count how many of each bracket must go, then search with that exact budget
body: A string with letters and round brackets is *valid* if the brackets are balanced. We may delete brackets (never letters) and we want to delete as **few** as possible. First one pass finds how many `(` and how many `)` have to be removed: scan the string with a balance counter; a `)` that finds the balance at 0 is surplus (`right += 1`); at the end the balance that is left over are surplus `(` (`left`).

Then a search decides for each character: **remove it** (only if the budget of that bracket is not used up) or **keep it**. The kept brackets must never let the balance go below zero. At the end of the string the budgets must both be 0 and the balance must be 0.

Different removals can give the **same** string (removing the first or the second of two equal brackets), so the results are kept in a set. Because the budget is exact, the search never goes deeper into a branch that would delete more than the minimum.

statement: A string contains lowercase letters and the brackets `(` and `)`. Delete the smallest possible number of brackets so that the brackets become balanced (every `(` has a matching later `)`, no `)` comes without an open `(`). Print all different strings that can result from a deletion of the smallest size, in ascending order (`(` comes before `)`, and both before letters), one per line. If the string is already balanced, print it as it is.
inputFormat: The only line has the string.
outputFormat: All different results in ascending order, one per line.
constraints: The string contains at least one letter, so no result is empty.

examples.note: One closing bracket is too many. Deleting the first ) gives (())()a; deleting the second or the third ) gives ()()()a.

hints: Count in one pass the number of surplus ( and ) that must be removed.
In the search, remove a bracket only while its budget is above zero, and keep a balance so that a kept ) always has an open (.
Store the results in a set, because equal brackets next to each other give the same string.

explanation: One scan counts the surplus brackets of each kind. The search keeps or removes every character, never removing more than the budget and never letting a kept `)` appear without an open `(`; complete balanced strings with the budgets used up are collected in a set.
solution.complexity: Time exponential in the number of brackets, small for 20 characters; space O(n).
